FaceDetailer:

-CFG should be anywhere from 5.0-8.0.

-Lower denoise to stay more true to the original image. Start at .3.

-Increase 'guide size' for even better results.

-Works very well with PuLID!

Node Logic: 

This is everything working in the background. You can ignore it unless you feel like tinkering with the logic or adding a feature.

How to Use:
First, choose your main Mode:

1 for standard Image Generation.
2 for Animation.
3 for 3D Gen.

Then, choose the Type for that Mode:

If Mode is 1 (Image): then Type 1=Txt2Img, 2=Img2Img, 3=Inpaint, 4=Outpaint.
If Mode is 2 (Animation) then Type 1=Txt2Vid, 2=Img2Vid, 3=Vid2Vid.

nodes.title: MakeDawns Comfyui Studio Playground
widgets_values:
START HERE!

-Make sure to change the lite graph to "straight" instead of "spline" in the settings (bottom left) for a much cleaner look.

-Hit 'Run' to generate an image and load the models. First run takes the longest. After that any feature that isn't on will be bypassed.
You can find the results of all your generations in your ComfyUI_windows_portable\ComfyUI\output folder

ControlNet:

-Pick the preview input of the controlnet output you want to see in the Preview image. See title for specific previews ->


-To use the control net Enable the node in the 'features' group and turn the switch of the controlnet you want to use from the Multi-Controlnet Stack node to ON. Default is switch 1 Canny.

switch 1 = Canny

switch 2 = Depth

switch 3 = OpenPose

-You may need to adjust 'image size' in the main control to match your controlnet reference image for best results.

Main Control: 

-First, pick the 'Type' in the "Features" panel.

-T2I (1): PROMPT ONLY. Ignores all reference images.

-I2I (2): Load an image. Prompt transforms it. Adjust 'denoise' to control the amount of change. Lower denoise = closer to reference image. 0.7 is a good start.

-Inpaint (3): Load an image, right-click image -> 'Open in mask editor'. Draw on what you want to replace and type what you want to see in the 'Positive Prompt'. Denoise at 1.0

-Outpaint (4): Load an image. Use 'ImagePadForOutpaint' below to expand the canvas and type what you want to see in the extra space in the 'Positive Prompt'. Start Denoise to 1.0

-PuLID: Works by swapping the face of the image in your reference node to the final output. Pick a clear image of someones face and place it in the 'Controlnet, PuLID Reference' node.

-IPAdapter: Is a style transfer node. It will take the style of your 'IPAdapter reference' node  image and influence the final output with it. Note that a high weight will overbear most generations so keeping it low .1-.3 is a good start.

nodes.title: POSITIVE PROMPT
widgets_values: beautiful scenery nature glass bottle landscape, , purple galaxy bottle,

MAIN WORKFLOW!

Designed to be used from left to right.

1.Loaders: Pick your models here.

2.Features: Choose what you want to do here. Txt2Img, Img2Img, etc.

3.Main Control: Tweak your generation here.

4.Results: See your final image here.

5.(Optional) Node Logic: Look under the hood here if you're brave.

6. Use the Fast Groups Muter just below to enable or disable entire groups you don't intend to use.

Animation:

-To use animation just change the number from the Mode node in the "Features" group to 2.

-Txt2Vid: Set type to 1 and type what you want to see in your prompts.

-Img2Vid: Set type to 2 and Place the image you want animated in the 'Img2Vid Start Frame'. Denoise set to .5 to start. 'Animation Image Size' node needs to be = to 'the Start Frame' for best results.

-Vid2Vid: Set type to 3 and Unbypass the 'Load Video" node in the Loaders group w/ctrl+m. Place the file of the video you want to use as reference there and generate. Set denoise to .5 to start. Set your frame rate and animation length.

-You can change the size of the frames in the 'Animation Image Size' node. Its currently set at 768x768 for lower end GPUs.

-NOTE! Save Image node gets a small black box as an output so the batch of images don't override the MP4 file. Without this you'll get a bunch of images instead of a video file.
